title: Replace a general host-coupled operator with a device-native distribution-equivalent primitive

source.title: SGLang PR #38117 and sealed local temporal reproduction
source.claim_scope: A merged categorical-sampling rewrite plus local operator-level evidence; transfer requires a fresh workload contract and target-hardware qualification.

required_capabilities: A device-native construction that preserves the required output distribution or mathematical contract.
A guarded fallback for deterministic, unsupported, or regression-prone modes.
dtypes: any, subject to numerical and statistical qualification
problem_signatures: host-coupled operator in an accelerator critical path
general operator performs stronger validation or bookkeeping than the local contract requires
small repeated GPU operation dominated by dispatch or framework overhead
output contract permits distributional rather than sample-by-sample equivalence

implementation_recipe: Write the narrow local semantic contract first, including whether equivalence is exact, numerical, set-valued, or distributional.
Decompose the general operator into mandatory work, validation, host bookkeeping, temporary materialization, and reduction steps.
Search for a device-native mathematical reformulation that removes non-mandatory host or framework work while preserving the declared equivalence class.
Retain deterministic and unsupported branches unchanged, and add an explicit rollout or fallback guard.
After the first correct material candidate, inspect remaining temporaries and algebraically equivalent score directions for in-place reuse, but keep dtype and rounding semantics explicit.
Route the candidate only to workloads where the removed work is a material part of the end-to-end critical path.
validation_recipe: Match the correctness test to the equivalence class: exact comparisons for deterministic paths and seeded statistical goodness-of-fit for stochastic paths.
Exercise zero, extreme, tied, non-contiguous, dtype, shape, and output-ABI cases, plus every retained fallback branch.
Test eager execution and CUDA Graph capture separately because launch removal changes the bottleneck and can reverse small-shape rankings.
Measure randomized interleaved shape points and reject universal routing when any important workload region regresses.
Measure whole-model latency or throughput before claiming transfer from the isolated operator.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Host dispatch and general validation cease to dominate, exposing random generation, elementwise scoring, reduction, and memory allocation.
CUDA Graph capture can erase much of the launch-side opportunity, making kernel count and device work decisive.
Low-precision key generation may trade speed for changed tie frequency or distribution bias.
failure_modes: Testing stochastic outputs for token identity instead of distributional equivalence.
Changing the seeded deterministic branch or random-number consumption contract unintentionally.
Using FP16 or BF16 random keys without testing quantization, ties, zeros, and high-cardinality bias.
Assuming eager rankings transfer to captured execution.
Optimizing an operator that is no longer material in the full model.
Treating one architecture's crossover point as a hardware-independent rule.
scope_limits: This method supplies a search transformation, not proof of a global optimum.
Distributional equivalence is admissible only when the operator contract explicitly permits it.
Source-reported model throughput and local operator measurements are priors, not target-run evidence.
Exact RNG sequence compatibility may be stricter than output-distribution compatibility and must be specified separately.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: A general operator combines mandatory mathematical work with host bookkeeping, validation, or temporary materialization that is unnecessary under the frozen local contract.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: Independent output rows or requests, with a device-native local construction per row.
local_state: Input row and its validity invariants.
Random or deterministic key state required by the equivalent construction.
A row-local reduction accumulator or candidate index.
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Reduce each row's equivalent scores using the operator-specific associative or selection rule.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Emit the same ABI and the declared exact, numerical, or distributional result class; route unsupported modes to the baseline.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Usually preserves mandatory asymptotic data work while removing constant host, validation, allocation, or materialization costs.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: One device construction followed by the reformulated row reduction, without host synchronization in the critical path.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: At minimum read the input and emit one result per row; reformulations may add a temporary key tensor unless fused or reused in place.
invariants: The selected equivalence class is frozen before optimization.
Each row is independent unless the original contract states otherwise.
Fallback paths preserve unsupported and deterministic semantics.
anti_patterns: Replacing a precise contract with a weaker stochastic claim after observing performance.
Copying the source implementation without decomposing the next exposed bottleneck.
Promoting a fast low-precision variant before high-cardinality bias and tie behavior are measured.

candidate_archetypes.name: device-native random-key reduction
candidate_archetypes.template: Replace a host-coupled categorical or ranking primitive with independent device-side random keys and a row reduction after proving the required distributional identity.

candidate_archetypes.name: in-place reciprocal score
candidate_archetypes.template: Rewrite score = probability / key, argmax as score = key / probability, argmin so the random workspace can hold scores in place, subject to zero, dtype, tie, and RNG-contract checks.

candidate_archetypes.name: execution-mode and shape router
candidate_archetypes.template: Dispatch the reformulation only in measured workload regions and retain the baseline for deterministic, unsupported, or regressing regions.
